content_full:
# Development Environment Setup

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| Node.js | >= 18.x | Runtime |
| **pnpm** | >= 9.x | Package manager (required — replaces npm) |
| PostgreSQL | >= 15.x | Database |
| Git | >= 2.x | Version control |

**Important:** This is a **pnpm workspace monorepo**. Do not use `npm install` per directory. Always use `pnpm install` from the project root. See [Monorepo Workflow](#monorepo-workflow) for details.

### Installing Prerequisites

**macOS:**
```bash
# Install Node.js via nvm
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.0/install.sh | bash
nvm install 18
nvm use 18

# Install pnpm
npm install -g pnpm

# Install PostgreSQL via Homebrew
brew install postgresql@15
brew services start postgresql@15
```

**Ubuntu/Debian:**
```bash
# Install Node.js
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_18.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt-get install -y nodejs

# Install pnpm
npm install -g pnpm

# Install PostgreSQL
sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-15
sudo systemctl start postgresql
```

**Windows:**
- Download Node.js from https://nodejs.org/
- Install pnpm: `npm install -g pnpm`
- Download PostgreSQL from https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
- Use PowerShell or Git Bash for command-line operations

## Monorepo Workflow

This project uses **Turborepo** for build orchestration and **pnpm workspaces** for dependency management.

```bash
# ONE command installs all dependencies for all workspaces
pnpm install

# Never do this (outdated per-directory approach)
# cd backend && npm install
# cd crm-frontend && npm install
```

Run tasks from the **project root** using Turborepo:

```bash
pnpm dev         # Start all services (Turbo handles parallelism)
pnpm build       # Build all apps (Turbo caches and manages order)
pnpm test        # Run all tests
pnpm lint        # Lint all workspaces
pnpm typecheck   # Type check all workspaces
```

To target a specific workspace:

```bash
pnpm dev:backend        # Start only the backend
pnpm dev:crm            # Start only the CRM admin
pnpm --filter backend test    # Run backend tests only
turbo build --filter=crm-frontend   # Build CRM only
```

## Project Setup

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd boomerang_project
```

### 2. Install All Dependencies

```bash
# One command installs everything across all workspaces
pnpm install
```

pnpm will install dependencies for the backend, all frontends, and all shared packages in `packages/`. This takes ~60 seconds on first run.

### 3. Configure Environment Variables

```bash
# Backend
cd backend
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `backend/.env` with your local settings. See [environment-variables.md](environment-variables.md) for full reference.

Minimum required:
```env
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/boomerang_crm?schema=public"
JWT_SECRET="your-local-dev-secret-key-min-32-chars"
PORT=3001
FRONTEND_URL="http://localhost:3000"
```

### 4. Set Up the Database

```bash
# From project root — Turborepo routes to the correct workspace
pnpm db:generate    # Generate Prisma client from schema

pnpm db:migrate     # Apply migrations (creates DB tables)

pnpm db:seed        # Seed reference/lookup data
```

To manually create the database if it does not exist:
```bash
psql -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE boomerang_crm;"
```

See [database.md](database.md) for detailed database setup.

### 5. Start Development Servers

```bash
# Option A: Start everything at once (recommended)
pnpm dev

# Option B: Start services individually in separate terminals
pnpm dev:backend       # Terminal 1 — NestJS API
pnpm dev:crm           # Terminal 2 — CRM Admin
pnpm dev:cms           # Terminal 3 — CMS Admin
pnpm dev:public        # Terminal 4 — Public Website
pnpm dev:student       # Terminal 5 — Student Portal
```

- **CRM Admin:** http://localhost:3000
- **Backend API:** http://localhost:3001
- **CMS Admin:** http://localhost:3002
- **Public Website:** http://localhost:3003
- **Student Portal:** http://localhost:3004
- **Swagger UI:** http://localhost:3001/api
- **Prisma Studio:** `pnpm db:studio` (opens in browser)

## Development Workflow

### Running Tests

```bash
# All tests (from project root via Turborepo)
pnpm test

# Specific workspace tests
pnpm --filter backend test
pnpm --filter backend test:e2e
```

### Code Quality

```bash
# Lint all workspaces
pnpm lint

# TypeScript type checking all workspaces
pnpm typecheck

# Format all code
pnpm format
```

### Database Migrations

```bash
# From project root (Turborepo routes to backend workspace)

# Create and apply a new migration
pnpm --filter backend prisma migrate dev --name add_new_column_to_students

# Shorthand
pnpm db:migrate

# Apply migrations in production (no schema changes)
pnpm db:migrate:deploy

# Open Prisma Studio (visual DB browser)
pnpm db:studio
```

### Working with Shared Packages

```typescript
// Import from shared packages — never from local paths
import type { Institution } from '@boomerang/types';  // Correct
import type { Institution } from '@/types';            // Do not do this

import { apiClient } from '@boomerang/api-client';    // Correct
import { apiClient } from '../lib/api';               // Do not do this
```

### Git Workflow

1. Create a feature branch from `main`: `git checkout -b feature/institution-activation`
2. Make changes and commit with descriptive messages (use conventional commits)
3. Run preflight: `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`
4. Push and create a pull request

## IDE Setup

### VS Code (Recommended)

Install these extensions:
- **ESLint** - Linting
- **Prettier** - Code formatting
- **TypeScript Importer** - Auto-import
- **PostgreSQL** - Database explorer
- **REST Client** - API testing

Recommended `settings.json`:
```json
{
  "editor.formatOnSave": true,
  "editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
  "typescript.preferences.importModuleSpecifier": "relative"
}
```

### WebStorm

- Enable ESLint: Settings -> Languages & Frameworks -> JavaScript -> Code Quality Tools -> ESLint
- Enable Prettier: Settings -> Languages & Frameworks -> JavaScript -> Prettier
- Database: Settings -> Database -> Add PostgreSQL datasource

## Debugging

### API Server

Add to VS Code `launch.json`:
```json
{
  "type": "node",
  "request": "launch",
  "name": "Debug API",
  "program": "${workspaceFolder}/src/api/server.ts",
  "runtimeArgs": ["-r", "tsx/cjs"],
  "env": {
    "NODE_ENV": "development"
  }
}
```

### Database Queries

Enable query logging in development:
```env
DB_DEBUG=true
```

This logs all SQL queries to the console via Knex.js debug mode.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|---------|
| Port 3000 already in use | `lsof -ti :3000 \| xargs kill` or change `PORT` in `backend/.env` |
| Database connection refused | Ensure PostgreSQL is running: `brew services start postgresql@15` |
| Migration fails | Check `DATABASE_URL` in `backend/.env`, ensure database exists |
| TypeScript errors in IDE | Run `pnpm typecheck` from root to see actual errors |
| Admin UI blank page | Check browser console for errors, ensure backend API is running |
| `Cannot find module '@boomerang/types'` | Run `pnpm install` from root — workspace links may be stale |
| `pnpm: command not found` | Install pnpm: `npm install -g pnpm` |
| Turbo cache issues | Run `pnpm clean` to clear all caches and rebuild |
| Prisma client out of date | Run `pnpm db:generate` after any schema.prisma changes |

title: Environment Variables
content_full:
# Environment Variables

All configuration is managed through environment variables. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust values for your environment.

## Required Variables

| Variable | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/boomerang_crm?schema=public` | Prisma database connection string |
| `JWT_SECRET` | `a-random-string-at-least-32-chars-long` | Secret key for signing JWT tokens |
| `PORT` | `3001` | Backend API server port |
| `FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` | Admin UI URL (for CORS) |

**Note:** All backend variables go in `backend/.env`. The frontend uses `crm-frontend/.env.local` for any frontend-specific env vars.

## Database

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | — | Prisma connection string: `postgresql://user:pass@host:port/db?schema=public` |

Prisma uses the single `DATABASE_URL` connection string. Append `?schema=public` for PostgreSQL.

## Authentication

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `JWT_SECRET` | — | JWT signing secret (min 32 characters) |
| `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` | `24h` | Access token expiry duration |

## Server

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `PORT` | `3001` | Backend API server port |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | Environment: `development` / `production` / `test` |
| `FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` | Admin UI URL (for CORS configuration) |

## Email (Notifications)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `SMTP_HOST` | — | SMTP server host |
| `SMTP_PORT` | `587` | SMTP port |
| `SMTP_USER` | — | SMTP username |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | — | SMTP password |
| `SMTP_FROM_EMAIL` | `noreply@boomerang.co.il` | Sender email address |
| `SMTP_FROM_NAME` | `Boomerang` | Sender display name |
| `SMTP_SECURE` | `false` | Use TLS (set `true` for port 465) |

## WhatsApp / SMS (Twilio)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` | — | Twilio account SID |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | — | Twilio auth token |
| `TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM` | — | WhatsApp sender number (e.g., `whatsapp:+14155238886`) |
| `TWILIO_SMS_FROM` | — | SMS sender number |

## File Uploads

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `UPLOAD_DIR` | `./uploads` | Local upload directory |
| `MAX_FILE_SIZE` | `10485760` | Max file size in bytes (10MB) |
| `ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES` | `pdf,jpg,jpeg,png` | Comma-separated allowed extensions |

## Logging

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | Log level: `error` / `warn` / `info` / `debug` |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | `json` | Log format: `json` / `pretty` |
| `LOG_FILE` | — | Log file path (optional, logs to stdout by default) |

## Admin UI

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `VITE_API_URL` | `http://localhost:3000/api/v1` | API base URL for the admin UI |

## Example .env File (`backend/.env`)

```env
# Database
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/boomerang_crm?schema=public"

# JWT
JWT_SECRET="your-secret-key-change-in-production"
JWT_EXPIRES_IN="24h"

# App
PORT=3001
NODE_ENV=development

# Frontend URL (for CORS)
FRONTEND_URL="http://localhost:3000"

# Email (SMTP) - optional for local dev
# SMTP_HOST="smtp.example.com"
# SMTP_PORT=587
# SMTP_USER="noreply@boomerang.co.il"
# SMTP_PASS="your-smtp-password"
# SMTP_FROM="Boomerang <noreply@boomerang.co.il>"

# WhatsApp/SMS (Twilio) - optional for local dev
# TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID="your-twilio-sid"
# TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN="your-twilio-token"
# TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER="+1234567890"
# TWILIO_WHATSAPP_NUMBER="whatsapp:+1234567890"
```

## Production Notes

- **Never commit `.env` to version control**
- Use a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, etc.) in production
- `JWT_SECRET` must be a cryptographically random string
- `DB_SSL=true` is required for remote database connections
- `NODE_ENV=production` enables performance optimizations
- `CORS_ORIGIN` should match the exact admin UI domain
- Set `LOG_LEVEL=warn` or `error` in production to reduce noise

# Testing Guide - Boomerang CRM

## Overview

The Boomerang CRM test suite uses a 4-layer testing strategy:

| Level | Tool | Directory | Speed |
|-------|------|-----------|-------|
| **Unit Tests** | Vitest | `tests/unit/` | Fast (< 30s) |
| **Integration Tests** | Vitest + Supertest | `tests/integration/` | Medium (1-3 min) |
| **Performance Tests** | Vitest | `tests/performance/` | Medium (1-2 min) |
| **E2E Tests** | Playwright | `tests/e2e/` | Slow (5-10 min) |

## Running Tests

```bash
# Run all tests (unit + integration + performance)
npm test

# Unit tests only
npm run test:unit

# Integration tests (requires PostgreSQL)
npm run test:integration

# Performance tests
npm run test:performance

# E2E tests (requires running API + UI servers)
npm run test:e2e

# E2E with interactive UI (for debugging)
npm run test:e2e:ui

# Watch mode (re-run on file changes)
npm run test:watch

# Coverage report
npm run test:coverage

# CI mode (verbose + coverage)
npm run test:ci
```

## Test Structure

```
tests/
  setup.ts                              # Global test setup (env vars, hooks)
  helpers/
    test-utils.ts                       # Factory functions, validators, helpers
    db-helpers.ts                       # Database cleanup, seeding utilities
  unit/
    validation.test.ts                  # Israeli ID, voucher codes, Hebrew text, enums
    auth.test.ts                        # JWT tokens, RBAC matrix, password security
    wallet.test.ts                      # Digital wallet balance logic, constraints
  integration/
    api-auth.test.ts                    # Login, token, protected routes
    api-institutions.test.ts            # Institution CRUD, status transitions, deals
    api-businesses.test.ts              # Business CRUD, voucher management
    api-students.test.ts                # Student lifecycle, wallet, enrollment
    api-support.test.ts                 # Support tickets, lotteries, groups, banks, insurance
    api-notifications.test.ts           # Notification triggers and scheduling
    api-reports.test.ts                 # All report endpoints per spec
    audit-log.test.ts                   # Audit logging for all operations
  e2e/
    auth-flows.spec.ts                  # Login/logout for all 3 roles
    institution-workflow.spec.ts        # Full institution lifecycle (potential->active->activated)
    student-workflow.spec.ts            # Full student lifecycle (register->enroll->wallet)
    business-voucher-workflow.spec.ts   # Business + voucher flows
    hebrew-rtl.spec.ts                  # Hebrew rendering, RTL layout, locale formatting
    reports.spec.ts                     # Report generation and CSV export
    support-ticket.spec.ts             # Support ticket create/respond/resolve
  performance/
    api-performance.test.ts             # Response time benchmarks, load testing
```

## Coverage Requirements

| Metric | Threshold |
|--------|-----------|
| Lines | 80% |
| Functions | 80% |
| Branches | 75% |
| Statements | 80% |

Coverage thresholds are enforced in `vitest.config.ts`. CI will fail if not met.

## Test Database Setup

Integration tests use a separate database: `boomerang_test`.

```bash
# Option 1: Docker (recommended)
docker run -d --name boomerang-test-db \n  -e POSTGRES_USER=postgres \n  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres \n  -e POSTGRES_DB=boomerang_test \n  -p 5432:5432 postgres:15

# Option 2: Local PostgreSQL
psql -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE boomerang_test;"

# Set environment
export TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/boomerang_test

# Run migrations and seed
npm run db:migrate
npm run db:seed
```

The test runner automatically:
1. Runs migrations before the test suite
2. Seeds reference data (study fields, categories, cities)
3. Cleans up data between tests using `cleanDatabase()` helper
4. Closes connections after the suite

## Test Helpers

### Factory Functions (`tests/helpers/test-utils.ts`)

```typescript
import {
  createTestStudent,
  createTestInstitution,
  createTestBusiness,
  createTestAdmin,
  createTestAreaManager,
  createTestOperations,
} from '../helpers/test-utils';

// All factories accept overrides
const student = createTestStudent({ first_name: 'Neta' });
const institution = createTestInstitution({ status: 'active' });
```

### Validators

```typescript
import {
  validateIsraeliId,
  validateVoucherCode,
  containsHebrew,
  isRTL,
} from '../helpers/test-utils';
```

### Assertion Helpers

```typescript
import {
  expectPaginatedResponse,
  expectErrorResponse,
  expectValidUUID,
  expectTimestamp,
} from '../helpers/test-utils';
```

### Database Helpers (`tests/helpers/db-helpers.ts`)

```typescript
import { cleanDatabase, seedLookupTables } from '../helpers/db-helpers';

beforeEach(async () => {
  await cleanDatabase(db);
  await seedLookupTables(db);
});
```

## Critical Workflows Tested

### 1. Institution: potential -> active -> activated (Flow 1)
- Form submission creates potential card with auto-email
- Deal status tracking (proposal_sent, phone_call, signed, dropped)
- Scheduled reminders (1 day, 2 days, 1 week)
- Operations converts to active (carries over all fields)
- Operations activates (visible on website, sends credentials email)

### 2. Business: potential -> active -> activated (Flow 2)
- Form submission creates potential card
- Business code assignment (2-letter English: e.g., HA)
- Voucher definition creation (3 types: specific_product, purchase_amount, percentage)
- Auto-generation of voucher codes (prefix + serial 01-10)
- Activation sends email with website link

### 3. Student: registration -> enrollment -> voucher redemption (Flow 3)
- Registration creates potential student with auto-generated personal code
- Personal URL generation
- Institution visit tracking via personal URL
- Conversion to active (THE critical step):
  - Creates enrollment record
  - Creates digital wallet with tuition credit
  - Records commission on institution card
  - Notifies accounting, institution, student
  - Updates mailing list
- Voucher redemption (debit wallet, record on 3 cards, notify)
- Savings plan enrollment (debit annual amount from wallet)
- Lottery ticket purchase (debit from wallet)

### 4. Support Ticket (Flow 9)
- Student creates ticket -> admin notified
- Admin responds (written or phone_call)
- Status flow: open -> in_progress -> resolved -> closed

## Hebrew/RTL Testing

Dedicated E2E suite (`tests/e2e/hebrew-rtl.spec.ts`):
- HTML `dir="rtl"` and `lang="he"` attributes
- Hebrew navigation menu items
- Hebrew table headers
- Hebrew text input and search
- Israeli date format (DD/MM/YYYY or D.M.YYYY)
- ILS currency display
- Mixed Hebrew-English rendering (URLs, codes)

## Israeli-Specific Validations

- **Israeli ID (Teudat Zehut)**: Luhn-like check digit algorithm (9 digits)
- **Phone numbers**: Israeli format `0XX-XXXXXXX`
- **Date formatting**: Hebrew locale `he-IL`
- **Voucher codes**: `BO` + business code + amount code + `-` + serial (01-10)
- **Personal codes**: `BOO` + 5+ digit auto-increment

## Performance Benchmarks

| Endpoint Type | Target |
|--------------|--------|
| Simple queries (list, get by ID) | < 200ms |
| Complex queries (reports, filtered search) | < 500ms |
| 10 concurrent list requests | All succeed |
| 50 concurrent read requests | All < 500ms |
| 5 concurrent write requests | No conflicts |

## CI/CD Pipeline

Tests run on every push/PR via `.github/workflows/test.yml`:

1. **Unit Tests** - No dependencies, runs first
2. **Integration Tests** - PostgreSQL service, needs unit tests passing
3. **Performance Tests** - PostgreSQL service, needs integration passing
4. **E2E Tests** - Full stack + Playwright, needs integration passing
5. **Coverage Report** - Generated as artifact (HTML + LCOV)

title: Production Deployment Guide
content_full:
# Production Deployment Guide

## Server Requirements

### Minimum (up to 1,000 entities)

| Resource | Minimum |
|----------|---------|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| RAM | 4 GB |
| Disk | 40 GB SSD |
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS |
| Node.js | 18.x LTS |
| PostgreSQL | 15.x |

### Recommended (up to 10,000 entities)

| Resource | Recommended |
|----------|-------------|
| CPU | 4 vCPU |
| RAM | 8 GB |
| Disk | 100 GB SSD |
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS |
| Node.js | 18.x LTS |
| PostgreSQL | 15.x |

## Architecture Overview

```
                    [Cloudflare / DNS]
                           |
                    [Nginx Reverse Proxy]
                      /           \n              [API Server]    [Admin UI Static]
              (Node.js)       (Nginx serves)
                    |
              [PostgreSQL]
```

## Step-by-Step Deployment

### 1. Provision Server

Choose a cloud provider (AWS EC2, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, etc.) and create a server with the recommended specs.

```bash
# Update system
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Install essentials
sudo apt install -y curl wget git build-essential nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx
```

### 2. Install Node.js

```bash
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_18.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt install -y nodejs
node --version  # Verify 18.x
```

### 3. Install and Configure PostgreSQL

```bash
sudo apt install -y postgresql-15

# Create database and user
sudo -u postgres psql << 'EOF'
CREATE USER boomerang WITH PASSWORD 'STRONG_PASSWORD_HERE';
CREATE DATABASE boomerang_crm OWNER boomerang;
\c boomerang_crm
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto";
EOF

# Configure for production
sudo nano /etc/postgresql/15/main/postgresql.conf
```

Key PostgreSQL settings (adjust for your RAM):
```ini
shared_buffers = 2GB            # 25% of RAM
effective_cache_size = 6GB      # 75% of RAM
work_mem = 32MB
maintenance_work_mem = 512MB
wal_buffers = 16MB
checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9
random_page_cost = 1.1
effective_io_concurrency = 200
max_connections = 100
log_min_duration_statement = 200
```

```bash
sudo systemctl restart postgresql
```

### 4. Deploy Application Code

```bash
# Install pnpm globally
npm install -g pnpm

# Create application user
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash boomerang

# Clone repository
sudo -u boomerang git clone <repository-url> /home/boomerang/app
cd /home/boomerang/app

# Install all workspace dependencies (pnpm handles the entire monorepo)
sudo -u boomerang pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# Build all apps (Turborepo orchestrates in dependency order)
sudo -u boomerang pnpm build

# Alternatively, build individual apps
sudo -u boomerang turbo build --filter=backend
sudo -u boomerang turbo build --filter=crm-frontend
```

### 5. Configure Environment Variables

```bash
sudo -u boomerang nano /home/boomerang/app/.env
```

```env
# Production settings
NODE_ENV=production
PORT=3000

# Database
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://boomerang:STRONG_PASSWORD_HERE@localhost:5432/boomerang_crm
DB_SSL=false
DB_POOL_MIN=5
DB_POOL_MAX=20

# Authentication
JWT_SECRET=CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY_RANDOM_64_CHAR_STRING
JWT_EXPIRY=24h
REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY=7d
BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12

# CORS (your admin UI domain)
CORS_ORIGIN=https://admin.boomerang.co.il

# Email
SMTP_HOST=smtp.provider.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=notifications@boomerang.co.il
SMTP_PASSWORD=EMAIL_PASSWORD
SMTP_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@boomerang.co.il
SMTP_FROM_NAME=Boomerang

# WhatsApp / SMS
TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=your_account_sid
TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=your_auth_token
TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM=whatsapp:+14155238886
TWILIO_SMS_FROM=+14155238886

# Logging
LOG_LEVEL=warn
LOG_FORMAT=json
LOG_FILE=/home/boomerang/logs/app.log

# Rate Limiting
RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW=60000
RATE_LIMIT_MAX=100
LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=5
```

### 6. Run Database Migrations

```bash
cd /home/boomerang/app
sudo -u boomerang npm run db:migrate
sudo -u boomerang npm run db:seed
```

### 7. Set Up Process Manager (PM2)

```bash
sudo npm install -g pm2

# Start the API server
sudo -u boomerang pm2 start src/api/server.ts \n  --name boomerang-api \n  --interpreter tsx \n  --max-memory-restart 1G

# Save PM2 process list
sudo -u boomerang pm2 save

# Enable PM2 startup on reboot
pm2 startup systemd -u boomerang --hp /home/boomerang
```

PM2 ecosystem file (`ecosystem.config.js`):
```javascript
module.exports = {
  apps: [{
    name: 'boomerang-api',
    script: 'src/api/server.ts',
    interpreter: 'tsx',
    instances: 2,
    exec_mode: 'cluster',
    max_memory_restart: '1G',
    env: {
      NODE_ENV: 'production',
    },
  }],
};
```

### 8. Configure Nginx

```bash
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/boomerang
```

```nginx
# API server
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name api.boomerang.co.il;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;

        # File upload limit
        client_max_body_size 10M;
    }
}

# Admin UI
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name admin.boomerang.co.il;

    root /home/boomerang/app/admin-ui/dist;
    index index.html;

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }

    # Cache static assets
    location ~* \.(js|css|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|ico|svg|woff|woff2)$ {
        expires 30d;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
    }
}
```

```bash
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/boomerang /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

### 9. SSL Certificates (Let's Encrypt)

```bash
sudo certbot --nginx -d api.boomerang.co.il -d admin.boomerang.co.il

# Auto-renewal is set up automatically
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
```

### 10. Set Up Automated Backups

```bash
# Create backup directory
sudo mkdir -p /home/boomerang/backups

# Create backup script
sudo nano /home/boomerang/backup.sh
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
BACKUP_DIR=/home/boomerang/backups
DB_NAME=boomerang_crm

# Create backup
pg_dump -U boomerang -h localhost -Fc $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_DIR/boomerang_$TIMESTAMP.dump

# Delete backups older than 30 days
find $BACKUP_DIR -name "boomerang_*.dump" -mtime +30 -delete

echo "Backup completed: boomerang_$TIMESTAMP.dump"
```

```bash
chmod +x /home/boomerang/backup.sh

# Add to crontab (daily at 2 AM)
sudo -u boomerang crontab -e
# Add: 0 2 * * * /home/boomerang/backup.sh >> /home/boomerang/logs/backup.log 2>&1
```

### 11. Set Up Log Rotation

```bash
sudo nano /etc/logrotate.d/boomerang
```

```
/home/boomerang/logs/*.log {
    daily
    missingok
    rotate 14
    compress
    delaycompress
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
```

## Monitoring

### PM2 Monitoring

```bash
# Real-time process status
pm2 status

# Live logs
pm2 logs boomerang-api

# Process metrics
pm2 monit
```

### Health Check Endpoint

The API exposes a health check at `GET /health`:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "database": "connected",
  "uptime": 86400
}
```

Set up a monitoring service (UptimeRobot, Pingdom, etc.) to check this endpoint every 1-5 minutes.

### Database Monitoring

```bash
# Check database size
sudo -u postgres psql -c "SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size('boomerang_crm'));"

# Check active connections
sudo -u postgres psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'boomerang_crm';"
```

## Updating the Application

```bash
# Pull latest code
cd /home/boomerang/app
sudo -u boomerang git pull origin main

# Install any new dependencies (pnpm handles all workspaces)
sudo -u boomerang pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# Run database migrations
sudo -u boomerang pnpm db:migrate:deploy

# Rebuild all apps (Turborepo only rebuilds what changed, using cache)
sudo -u boomerang pnpm build

# Restart API server (zero-downtime with PM2 cluster mode)
sudo -u boomerang pm2 reload boomerang-api
```

Turborepo caches build results. On subsequent deployments, only changed apps and their dependents are rebuilt:

```bash
# First deployment: full build (~5 minutes)
pnpm build

# Second deployment with no code changes: instant (cache hit)
pnpm build

pnpm build
```

sudo -u boomerang git checkout <previous-commit-hash>

| SSL certificate expired | `sudo certbot certificates` | `sudo certbot renew` |
| Disk space full | `df -h` | Clean logs, old backups |
| High memory usage | `pm2 monit` | Restart, check for memory leaks |
| Slow queries | Check `LOG_FILE` | Add indexes, optimize queries |
| Login not working | Check JWT_SECRET consistency | Ensure same secret across restarts |

- [ ] All passwords changed from defaults
- [ ] `.env` file has restrictive permissions (`chmod 600`)
- [ ] PostgreSQL only accepts local connections (or SSL for remote)
- [ ] Nginx configured with security headers
- [ ] SSL/TLS enabled with strong ciphers
- [ ] Firewall configured (only ports 80, 443, 22)
- [ ] SSH key-based authentication (password auth disabled)
- [ ] Automated backups running and tested
- [ ] Log rotation configured
- [ ] Rate limiting enabled
- [ ] CORS restricted to admin UI domain

# Implementation Summary -- Boomerang CRM Platform
## Executive Report -- February 16, 2026

**Project:** Boomerang CRM (NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL + 4 Next.js frontends)
**Date:** 2026-02-16
**Prepared by:** SR-TW (Agent #178, Documentation Department 20)

---

## Overview

Four major engineering phases were executed in a single coordinated session, transforming the Boomerang CRM platform from an early prototype into a hardened, tested, and well-architected system. The work spanned frontend state management, backend security, API quality assurance, and critical bug resolution.

**Total impact:** 60+ files modified or created across the full stack, 10 security vulnerabilities remediated, 146 API tests executed, and 2 critical bugs fixed.

---

## Phase Summary

| Phase | Scope | Key Metric | Status |
|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 1. Zustand State Management | 3 frontend apps | 5 stores created, 8 files migrated | Complete |
| 2. Security Audit & Hardening | Backend + config | 10 vulnerabilities fixed (3 Critical, 4 High, 3 Medium) | Complete (manual credential rotation pending) |
| 3. API QA Testing | 132 endpoints | 146 tests, 84.2% pass rate, 9 bugs found | Complete |
| 4. Bug Fixes | Backend controllers + services | 2 P0 bugs resolved | Complete |

---

## Phase 1: Zustand State Management Migration

**Objective:** Replace scattered `useState` and direct `localStorage` calls across three Next.js applications with centralized zustand stores.

**Architecture decisions:**
- `persist` middleware for auth stores (survives page refresh)
- In-memory only for sensitive data (student activation passwords)
- Thin `useAuth()` hook wrappers for backward compatibility
- Separate storage keys per app (`boomerang-crm-auth`, `boomerang-cms-auth`, `boomerang-student-auth`)

**Stores created:**

| Store | App | Purpose | Persistence |
|-------|-----|---------|-------------|
| `authStore` | CRM Frontend | User auth, JWT tokens, role checking | localStorage |
| `authStore` | CMS Admin | Admin auth, JWT tokens, role checking | localStorage |
| `authStore` | Student Portal | Student auth, personal code login | localStorage |
| `uiStore` | CRM Frontend | Toast notification queue | In-memory |
| `studentStore` | CRM Frontend | Activation credential cache | In-memory (security) |

**Files created or modified:** 11 files across `crm-frontend/`, `cms-admin/`, `student-portal/`

**Key detail:** The `studentStore` deliberately avoids `persist` middleware. Activation passwords are sensitive credentials that must not be written to `localStorage`. They exist only for the duration of the CRM session and are cleared on navigation away.

---

## Phase 2: Security Audit & Hardening

**Objective:** Identify and remediate security vulnerabilities across the entire backend.

**Audit methodology:** Manual code review, static analysis of authentication flows, configuration file inspection, git history analysis for secrets, STRIDE threat modeling.

**Findings and fixes:**

| # | Severity | Finding | Fix |
|---|----------|---------|-----|
| 1 | CRITICAL | Plaintext passwords in database | Bcrypt hashing (12 rounds) for all password storage |
| 2 | CRITICAL | Hardcoded JWT secret in repository | `.env.example` with generation guidance, `.gitignore` updated |
| 3 | CRITICAL | `.env` not in `.gitignore` | Added all `.env` variants to `.gitignore` |
| 4 | HIGH | `Math.random()` for password generation | Replaced with `crypto.randomInt()` / `crypto.randomBytes()` |
| 5 | HIGH | No bcrypt for institution passwords | Bcrypt comparison with auto-migration on first login |
| 6 | HIGH | Swagger exposed in production | Environment-gated: disabled by default in production |
| 7 | HIGH | Overly permissive CORS | Configurable origin allowlist with safe defaults |
| 8 | MEDIUM | Missing Prisma `directUrl` | Added for secure migration execution |
| 9 | MEDIUM | No `.env.example` guidance | Created comprehensive examples with secret generation commands |
| 10 | MEDIUM | Password fields in API responses | Excluded via destructuring before returning responses |

**Additional security controls implemented:**
- JWT secret strength validation at startup (rejects weak/short secrets)
- Security headers middleware (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options)
- Account lockout after 5 failed login attempts (15-minute lockout)
- `@Public()` decorator for explicit public route marking
- Admin-only registration endpoint protection
- JWT account status validation on every request
- Rate limiting on authentication and public registration endpoints
- Mass assignment protection via field whitelisting in update operations

**Compliance impact:** Remediation addresses GDPR Article 32 (security of processing), Israeli Privacy Protection Law database security requirements, and OWASP Top 10 (2021).

**Pending manual action:** All credentials committed to git history must be rotated before production deployment. See `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/docs/security/ACTION-REQUIRED.md`.

---

## Phase 3: API QA Testing

**Objective:** Comprehensive API testing across all 132 endpoints in the backend.

**Execution model:** Three parallel QA agents with distinct scopes:
- Agent 1: Functional & integration testing (74 tests)
- Agent 2: Authentication & authorization testing (46 tests)
- Agent 3: Performance & load testing (26 tests)

**Results:**

| Stream | Tests | Passed | Failed | Pass Rate |
|--------|-------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Auth & Authorization | 46 | 38 | 8 | 82.6% |
| Functional & Integration | 74 | 63 | 11 | 85.1% |
| Performance & Load | 26 | 22 | 4 | 84.6% |
| **Total** | **146** | **123** | **23** | **84.2%** |

**Positive findings:**
- RBAC enforcement: 14/14 role-based tests passed
- Sensitive data handling: No password hashes or PII leaked in any response
- JWT security: Tampered, malformed, and missing tokens all properly rejected
- SQL injection prevention: Prisma ORM parameterizes all queries
- Performance under load: 50 concurrent requests handled in 511ms
- Average response time: ~430ms across all endpoints

**Bugs found:** 9 bugs identified (2 P0, 2 P1, 5 P2-P3). See Phase 4 for P0 resolution.

---

## Phase 4: Bug Fixes

**Objective:** Resolve the two P0 (critical) bugs blocking core business flows.

### BUG-002: Student Activation 500 Error (P0)
- **Symptom:** `POST /api/v1/students/:id/activate` returned 500 Internal Server Error
- **Root cause:** The `notificationsService.sendWelcomeEmail()` call threw an unhandled exception when the email transport was misconfigured or the Resend API key was invalid
- **Fix:** Wrapped the email send in a try/catch block. Activation now succeeds even if email delivery fails. The error is logged but does not block the core business operation.
- **File:** `backend/src/modules/students/students.service.ts:102-114`

### BUG-004: Public Endpoints Return 401 (P0)
- **Symptom:** `GET /api/v1/institutions`, `POST /api/v1/institutions`, `GET /api/v1/businesses`, `POST /api/v1/businesses` returned 401 Unauthorized without authentication
- **Root cause:** After the security hardening phase applied global `JwtAuthGuard`, the `@Public()` decorator was not applied to the correct controller methods for institutions and businesses
- **Fix:** Added `@Public()` decorator to the `create()` and `findAll()` methods on `InstitutionsController` and `BusinessesController`
- **Files:** `backend/src/modules/institutions/institutions.controller.ts`, `backend/src/modules/businesses/businesses.controller.ts`

---

## Departments and Agents Involved

| Department | Agent Code | Role | Contribution |
|-----------|-----------|------|-------------|
| Engineering (02) | CTO (#102) | Architecture Lead | Zustand architecture blueprint, implementation coordination |
| Engineering (02) | Engineering Lead | Implementation | Zustand stores, security fixes, bug fixes |
| QA (07) | COO | QA Lead | Test plan creation, test execution coordination, results analysis |
| QA (07) | Functional QA Agent | Tester | 74 functional and integration tests |
| QA (07) | Auth QA Agent | Tester | 46 authentication and authorization tests |
| QA (07) | Performance QA Agent | Tester | 26 performance and load tests |
| Security (08) | CISO (#134) | Security Lead | Security audit coordination |
| Security (08) | API Security Agent | Specialist | API security review |
| Security (08) | DB Security Agent | Specialist | Database security review |
| Security (08) | Web Security Agent | Specialist | Web application security review |
| Security (08) | Auth Security Agent | Specialist | Authentication security review |
| Security (08) | Crypto Security Agent | Specialist | Cryptography and secrets review |
| Security (08) | Input Validation Agent | Specialist | Input validation and output encoding review |
| Documentation (20) | SR-TW (#178) | Senior Technical Writer | This documentation |

---

## Remaining Issues

### Must Fix Before Production
1. **Rotate all credentials** committed to git history (JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, API keys)
2. **BUG-001:** Audit log endpoint returns 500 (BigInt serialization issue) -- P1
3. **BUG-003:** Invalid enum values cause 500 instead of 400 -- P1

### Should Fix Soon
4. **BUG-005:** UpdateInstitutionDto and UpdateBusinessDto missing `notes` field -- P2
5. **BUG-007:** Seed students missing wallet records -- P3
6. **BUG-008:** User registration validation edge case -- P3

### Recommended Enhancements
7. Implement refresh tokens with rotation (currently using long-lived access tokens)
8. Add multi-factor authentication for admin users
9. Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection
10. Add Helmet.js for comprehensive security headers
11. Implement CI/CD security scanning pipeline

---

## File Impact Summary

**Files created:** ~15 new files (stores, hooks, decorators, DTOs, templates, env examples)
**Files modified:** ~45 files across backend and 3 frontend apps
**Files removed:** 51 test files (legacy test infrastructure cleanup)
**Net change:** ~61,270 lines added, ~9,413 lines removed

---

## Documentation Artifacts

| Document | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| This summary | `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-SUMMARY.md` | Executive overview of all work |
| Zustand migration guide | `docs/ZUSTAND-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` | Developer guide for zustand implementation |
| Security audit report | `docs/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` | Detailed security findings |
| API test summary | `docs/API-TEST-SUMMARY.md` | QA testing results |
| Changelog | `docs/CHANGELOG.md` | Chronological list of all changes |
| Architecture decisions | `docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` | Key ADRs from this session |

---

See `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/docs/security/ACTION-REQUIRED.md`. --- ## Phase 3: API QA Testing **Objective:** Comprehensive API testing across all 132 endpoints in the backend. **Execution model:** Three parallel QA agents with distinct scopes: - Agent 1: Functional & integration testing (74 tests) - Agent 2: Authentication & authorization testing (46 tests) - Agent 3: Performance & load testing (26 tests) **Results:** | Stream | Tests | Passed | Failed | Pass Rate | |--------|-------|--------|--------|-----------| | Auth & Authorization | 46 | 38 | 8 | 82.6% | | Functional & Integration | 74 | 63 | 11 | 85.1% | | Performance & Load | 26 | 22 | 4 | 84.6% | | **Total** | **146** | **123** | **23** | **84.2%** | **Positive findings:** - RBAC enforcement: 14/14 role-based tests passed - Sensitive data handling: No password hashes or PII leaked in any response - JWT security: Tampered, malformed, and missing tokens all properly rejected - SQL injection prevention: Prisma ORM parameterizes all queries - Performance under load: 50 concurrent requests handled in 511ms - Average response time: ~430ms across all endpoints **Bugs found:** 9 bugs identified (2 P0, 2 P1, 5 P2-P3). See Phase 4 for P0 resolution. --- ## Phase 4: Bug Fixes **Objective:** Resolve the two P0 (critical) bugs blocking core business flows. ### BUG-002: Student Activation 500 Error (P0) - **Symptom:** `POST /api/v1/students/:id/activate` returned 500 Internal Server Error - **Root cause:** The `notificationsService.sendWelcomeEmail()` call threw an unhandled exception when the email transport was misconfigured or the Resend API key was invalid - **Fix:** Wrapped the email send in a try/catch block. Activation now succeeds even if email delivery fails. The error is logged but

does not block the core business operation. - **File:** `backend/src/modules/students/students.service.ts:102-114` ### BUG-004: Public Endpoints Return 401 (P0) - **Symptom:** `GET /api/v1/institutions`, `POST /api/v1/institutions`, `GET /api/v1/businesses`, `POST /api/v1/businesses` returned 401 Unauthorized without authentication - **Root cause:** After the security hardening phase applied global `JwtAuthGuard`, the `@Public()` decorator was not applied to the correct controller methods for institutions and businesses - **Fix:** Added `@Public()` decorator to the `create()` and `findAll()` methods on `InstitutionsController` and `BusinessesController` - **Files:** `backend/src/modules/institutions/institutions.controller.ts`, `backend/src/modules/businesses/businesses.controller.ts` --- ## title: Zustand Migration Guide - Boomerang CRM Platform
content_chunks: # Zustand Migration Guide -- Boomerang CRM Platform ## State Management Architecture & Developer Reference **Date:** 2026-02-16 **Author:** SR-TW (Agent #178, Documentation Department 20) **Applies to:** CRM Frontend, CMS Admin, Student Portal --- ## 1. Why Zustand The Boomerang platform has three Next.js frontend applications that previously managed auth state and UI state via scattered `useState` hooks and direct `localStorage` calls. This approach led to: - Duplicated auth logic across components - Inconsistent state after page refresh (manual `localStorage` parsing) - No single source of truth for authentication status - Sensitive data (passwords) accidentally persisted to browser storage Zustand was chosen for its minimal API surface, built-in persistence middleware, TypeScript support, and compatibility with Next.js server/client component boundaries. --- ## 2. Architecture Overview ``` +------------------+ +------------------+ +---------------------+ | CRM Frontend | | CMS Admin | | Student Portal | +------------------+ +------------------+ +---------------------+ | store/ | | store/ | | store/ | | authStore.ts | | authStore.ts | | authStore.ts | | uiStore.ts | +------------------+ +---------------------+ | studentStore.ts| | hooks/ | | hooks/ | +------------------+ | useAuth.ts | | useAuth.ts | | hooks/ | +------------------+ +---------------------+ | useAuth.ts | +------------------+ ``` **Pattern:** Each app has its own `store/` directory with zustand stores and a `hooks/` directory with thin wrapper hooks that select state from the stores. --- ## 3. Store Inventory ### 3.1 Auth Store (All Three Apps) **Files:** - `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/crm-frontend/src/store/authStore.ts` - `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/cms-admin/src/store/authStore.ts` - `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/student-portal/src/store/authStore.ts` **Purpose:** Centralized authentication state including user profile, JWT tokens, and auth status. **State shape (CRM & CMS):** ```typescript interface AuthStore { user: AuthUser | null; tokens: AuthTokens | null; isAuthenticated: boolean; isLoading: boolean; login: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<boolean>; logout: () => void; hasRole: (roles: UserRole[]) => boolean; setLoaded: () => void; } ``` **State shape (Student Portal):** ```typescript interface AuthStore { student: StudentUser | null; token: string | null; isAuthenticated: boolean; isLoading: boolean; login: (personalCode: string, password: string) => Promise<boolean>; logout: () => void; setLoaded: () => void; } ``` **Persistence:** All three auth stores use `persist` middleware with `localStorage`. **Storage keys:** - CRM: `boomerang-crm-auth` - CMS: `boomerang-cms-auth` - Student Portal: `boomerang-student-auth` **Rehydration:** Each store uses `onRehydrateStorage` to set `isLoading = false` and restore `isAuthenticated` based on the presence of user + token data after a page refresh. ### 3.2 UI Store (CRM Frontend Only) **File:** `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/crm-frontend/src/store/uiStore.ts` **Purpose:** Global toast notification queue, replacing the previous per-component `useState` approach. **State shape:** ```typescript interface UiStore { toasts: ToastMessage[]; addToast: (type: "success" | "error" | "info", message: string) => void; dismissToast: (id: string) => void; success: (message: string) => void; error: (message: string) => void; info: (message: string) => void; } ``` **Persistence:** None (in-memory only). Toasts are transient UI state. ### 3.3 Student Store (CRM Frontend Only) **File:** `/Users/kinghippo/Documents/boomerang_by_nexus/boomerang_project/crm-frontend/src/store/studentStore.ts` **Purpose:** Caches student activation credentials (generated password, personal code) for display in the CRM admin interface after activating a student. **State shape:** ```typescript interface StudentStore { activations: Record<string, StudentActivation>; setActivation: (studentId: string, data: StudentActivation) => void; getActivation: (studentId: string) => StudentActivation | null; clearActivation: (studentId: string) =>

void; } ``` **Persistence:** None. **This is a deliberate security decision.** Activation passwords are sensitive credentials and must never be written to `localStorage` or any persistent browser storage. They exist only for the duration of the current browser session. --- ## 4. Hook Wrappers Each app exposes a `useAuth()` hook that selects individual properties from the auth store. This provides a clean API for components and maintains backward compatibility with the previous `useState`-based `useAuth()` hook. **Pattern:** ```typescript // hooks/useAuth.ts "use client"; import { useAuthStore } from "@/store/authStore"; export function useAuth() { const user = useAuthStore((state) => state.user); const isAuthenticated = useAuthStore((state) => state.isAuthenticated); const login = useAuthStore((state) => state.login); const logout = useAuthStore((state) => state.logout); // ... return { user, isAuthenticated, login, logout }; } ``` **Why individual selectors instead of a single `useAuthStore()` call?** Zustand re-renders components only when the selected slice of state changes. Selecting individual properties prevents unnecessary re-renders. For example, a component that only reads `isAuthenticated` will not re-render when `isLoading` changes. The CRM frontend also provides a backward-compatible `useToast()` hook exported from `Toast.tsx`: ```typescript // components/ui/Toast.tsx export function useToast() { const toasts = useUiStore((state) => state.toasts); const addToast = useUiStore((state) => state.addToast); // ... return { messages: toasts, addToast, dismissToast, success, error, info }; } ``` --- ## 5. Usage Examples ### Login flow ```typescript "use client"; import { useAuth } from "@/hooks/useAuth"; export default function LoginPage() { const { login, isLoading, isAuthenticated } = useAuth(); const handleLogin = async (email: string, password: string) => { const success = await login(email, password); if (success) { router.push("/dashboard"); } }; } ``` ### Displaying toasts (CRM only) ```typescript import { useUiStore } from "@/store/uiStore"; function SaveButton() { const success = useUiStore((state) => state.success); const error = useUiStore((state) => state.error); const handleSave = async () => { try { await api.save(data); success("Saved successfully"); } catch { error("Failed to save"); } }; } ``` ### Caching activation credentials (CRM only) ```typescript import { useStudentStore } from "@/store/studentStore"; function ActivateButton({ studentId }: { studentId: string }) { const setActivation = useStudentStore((s) => s.setActivation); const handleActivate = async () => { const result = await api.activateStudent(studentId); setActivation(studentId, { studentId, personalCode: result.personalCode, generatedPassword: result.generatedPassword, activatedAt: new Date().toISOString(), }); }; } ``` --- ## 6. Adding New Stores Follow this pattern when adding a new zustand store: 1. Create `src/store/newStore.ts`: ```typescript import { create } from 'zustand'; interface NewStore { // State items: Item[]; // Actions addItem: (item: Item) => void; removeItem: (id: string) => void; } export const useNewStore = create<NewStore>()((set) => ({ items: [], addItem: (item) => set((state) => ({ items: [...state.items, item], })), removeItem: (id) => set((state) => ({ items: state.items.filter((i) => i.id !== id), })), })); ``` 2. If persistence is needed, wrap with `persist`: ```typescript import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware'; export const useNewStore = create<NewStore>()( persist( (set) => ({ /* ... */ }), { name: 'boomerang-[app]-[store]' } ) ); ``` 3. If a hook wrapper is desired for backward compatibility, create `src/hooks/useNew.ts`. **Do not persist sensitive data.**

Passwords, tokens with long lifetimes, PII, or financial data should use in-memory stores only. --- ## 7. Migration Checklist (For Future Components) When migrating a component from `useState` + `localStorage` to zustand: - [ ] Identify all `useState` calls related to the state being migrated - [ ] Identify all direct `localStorage.getItem/setItem` calls - [ ] Create the zustand store with the combined state shape - [ ] Create selector hooks for the state slices used by components - [ ] Replace `useState` calls with zustand selectors - [ ] Remove all direct `localStorage` calls (persist middleware handles this) - [ ] Remove any `useEffect` that syncs state to `localStorage` - [ ] Test that page refresh preserves auth state (for persisted stores) - [ ] Test that logout clears all persisted state - [ ] Verify no sensitive data is written to `localStorage` (check DevTools > Application > Local Storage) --- ## 8. Dependencies All three apps include zustand as a direct dependency: ```json { "dependencies": { "zustand": "^5.0.0" } } ``` No additional zustand plugins or middleware packages are required. The `persist` middleware is included in the core `zustand/middleware` module. --- **Document Owner:** SR-TW (Agent #178) -- Documentation Department 20 **Date:** 2026-02-16
